Computes typed coherence, explanatory-power, and global-theory-fit signals over the current web of claims.
Ranks the best conceptual entry points into the current problem state.
Turns entry points into ordered proof-pathway agendas.
Diagnoses why the target problem remains hard in the current conceptual regime.
Prioritizes bridge programs between the most consequential concepts and statements.
Conjectures the bridge objects or abstraction families that could close the strongest concept gaps.

phases.title: Foundational Definitions
phases.summary: st.def.compact-convex-set (definition): The theorem lives on a nonempty compact convex subset because averaging and compactness both need this ambient geometry.

phases.title: Affine Averaging
phases.summary: st.lem.cesaro-averages (lemma): Cesaro averages of a single affine orbit stay inside K and provide the averaging mechanism behind single-map fixed-point extraction.

phases.title: Single-Map Fixed-Point Extraction
phases.summary: st.lem.single-map-fixed-point (lemma): A single continuous affine self-map of a nonempty compact convex set has at least one fixed point.

phases.title: Invariant Fixed-Point Subset
phases.summary: st.prop.fixed-point-subset-structure (proposition): The [hidden bridge concept] of a single map is itself a nonempty compact convex set.

phases.title: Commuting Invariance
phases.summary: st.lem.commuting-preserves-fixed-point-subset (lemma): If two affine maps commute, then one preserves the [hidden bridge concept] of the other.

phases.title: Finite-Family Lift
phases.summary: st.lem.finite-family-common-fixed-point (lemma): One can build a common fixed point for any finite commuting subfamily by iteratively restricting to invariant [hidden bridge concept]s.

phases.title: Common Fixed-Point Theorem
phases.summary: st.thm.markov-kakutani (theorem): A commuting family of continuous affine self-maps on a nonempty compact convex set has a common fixed point.

phases.title: Examples and Interpretation
phases.summary: st.ex.interval-commuting-projections (example): On a compact interval, commuting affine self-maps illustrate the theorem in the simplest convex setting.
